brief: Oracle sent Project Jupiter's developer, a Blue Owl Capital unit, a force majeure notice citing permitting delays preventing it from securing power for the 2.45GW New Mexico data center before its first-phase deadline in the first half of 2027. Oracle publicly argued the notice does not establish a delay or change delivery expectations. Per FT sources, the contract still obligates Oracle to pay a ‘carry cost’ in lieu of rent for up to three years if the deadline is missed, covering debt holders’ interest in full plus a level of equity return to Blue Owl funds. One source said the power delivery risk sits with Oracle, not the investors. A second said there is disagreement over whether force majeure can be triggered before the project's scheduled completion date. Separately, the $18bn bank consortium funding construction (20+ banks led by BNP Paribas, Goldman Sachs, MUFG, SMBC) has failed to syndicate the debt more broadly on Oracle creditworthiness concerns, and the loans were already trading below 90 cents on the dollar. A gas pipeline meant to supply the site was pushed to February 2027, and OpenAI's other Stargate-linked project, SB Energy, separately delayed its IPO for similar reasons.
